result.title: MotionCore: A Latent Neural Simulator for Video Generation with Rigid-Body Dynamics
result.summary: Video generation models can produce highly realistic videos while generating physically inconsistent object motion. This limitation suggests that visual modeling alone may not provide a transferable representation of physical dynamics. We introduce MotionCore, a framework for learning physical dynamics via a learnable partial differential equation solver and focuses on rigid-body motion. We introduce a latent neural simulator learning to predict the evolution of object-level physical states from observed motion. Its predictions are then converted into spatially aligned latent controls for a controllable video diffusion model. The generator serves as a visual interface: it provides appearance and scene detail, while the learned dynamics model specifies the physical trajectory. To preserve this trajectory through the interface, MotionCore combines a diffusion-matching objective with a low-capacity decodability constraint on object identity and position. We evaluate MotionCore on public physical-consistency benchmarks and on paired data with known trajectories. Results indicate that MotionCore improves physical consistency and trajectory obedience in the evaluated rigid-body settings, while maintaining comparable visual quality. A controlled ablation protocol compares learned dynamics with an analytic prior and studies the choice of latent evolution processor.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 MotionCore，用可学习 PDE 求解器构建 latent 神经模拟器，从观测运动预测物体级物理状态的演化，再将其转为空间对齐的 latent 控制信号驱动视频扩散生成，并以 diffusion-matching 目标配合对物体身份与位置的低容量可解码性约束。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作并非 VLM 推理研究，但其把动力学状态与外观分离、并用低容量可解码性约束保留位置与身份信息的做法，可能为 LVR 中潜在状态是否保留几何与任务必要信息、如何抑制信息坍缩提供可供核查的训练线索。
